subject: physics
question_text: Why are pillars used in construction given distributed (widened) ends rather than rounded ends?

mark_split.label: Lower stress means a stronger pillar

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 9 Very Short Answer Question 14 (printed p.99). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: stress σ = F/A falls as the contact area A rises for the same load F, so a widened end lowers the stress a pillar's material feels at its top and bottom, keeping it further from the elastic limit — the standard NCERT reasoning for why pillars are built with distributed ends.

steps.label: Widened ends spread the load
lines: ends spreads its load over a large
A pillar with rounded ends carries

steps.why: The area a pillar's end presents to the load it carries is a matter of its shape alone, so widening the end is the direct way to change that area without changing the load.
common_mistakes: Saying a rounded end is weaker without naming the small contact area as the reason.
Describing the load without comparing the contact area of a widened end to that of a rounded end.
steps.memory_tip: Wide end, wide contact area; round end, a small point of contact.
steps.margin_note: Marked for naming the large contact area of a widened end against the small contact area of a rounded end.

steps.label: Lower stress means a stronger pillar
lines: Since stress σ = F/A, the same load
F on a larger area A gives a
smaller stress at a widened end

lines.text: σ = F/A: larger A gives smaller σ, same F
Wide ends stay below the elastic limit

steps.why: A pillar's material fails once its stress crosses the elastic limit, so keeping the stress at its ends low, by making the end wide, lets the pillar carry a larger load before that limit is reached.
common_mistakes: Saying wide ends are stronger without connecting it to the formula σ = F/A.
Claiming the load itself is smaller at a widened end. The load F is the same; only the area A, and so the stress, changes.
steps.memory_tip: Same weight, wider foot: the stress it feels drops, so it can carry more.
steps.margin_note: Marked for stating σ = F/A and that a larger area at the widened end gives a lower stress there.

insider_note: The second mark needs the stress formula tied to the contact area, not just a bare statement that wide ends are stronger.
